caption: sky note: "retrograde planets move backwards". not true. they only look like they do, from earth. jupiter stations retrograde in leo on dec 12.

slides.headline: does *jupiter* really move backwards on saturday?
“retrograde planets actually move backwards”
slides.body: no planet ever reverses its orbit. retrograde is how it looks from earth: we're moving too, so planets seem to slow, stop and loop back against the stars.

slides.headline: it is the *overtaking* effect
slides.body: earth orbits faster than jupiter and saturn. as we pass them, they seem to drift back, like a slower car as you overtake it.

slides.headline: retrograde reads as *review*, not disaster
slides.body: a time to revisit what that planet rules. saturn turns direct in aries on dec 10, jupiter retrograde in leo on dec 12.

slides.headline: a planet looking backwards isn't a reason to *text* backwards
